details: CONFIRMED by reading: finished_red() returns any non-zero exit of a log whose head is G and whose cmd matches, and run()
returns it before the lock; cmd_gate has no option that bypasses reuse (only --paid and -- <args>, which change the cmd
line). The result of a gate depends on more than the commit (the environment, installed tools, the gate script when it
lives outside the repo, machine load), and the merge hook already treats "red then green on the same code" as a real
sequence (merge.test.sh T15m2), so a re-run of the same code is a reachable, expected action; before this change it was
the default. The output is byte-identical to the first run (the new test asserts it), so neither a person nor a runner
can tell a reused red from a fresh one. The green case has the same silence, but a reused green is what the earlier
decision asked for; a reused red that was caused by the environment is wrong data.
Size: 20 minutes (a flag in cmd_gate threaded to run(), one printed line, skip 127 and >=128 in finished_red, 3 tests,
one sentence in delegate SKILL step 3).

failing_case: Worktree at G; `relay gate` runs and the gate command is killed by the OOM killer or a step times out under the load of
6 parallel gates (log ends `exit 137`, or `exit 1` with "tests FAILED (timeout)"), or a tool the gate needs was not
installed (`exit 127`, "gate command could not start"). The log is committed (HEAD = record commit R). The cause is
fixed outside the repository (tool installed, load gone). `relay gate` again: now prints the same
"gate G: exit 137" and the same lines in a second, runs nothing, and there is no flag to run it. Only a commit that
touches a file outside .relay/checks/ (or one that deletes the log) gets a real run; an empty commit does not
(its diff is empty, so the walk goes on). Should: a way to run the gate again on the same code, and a line saying the
result is a reused one, so a runner does not report "red again, reproduced".
Live in this change: tests/test_gate.py test_r4 on master changed the gate script outside the repo and expected the
rerun to exit 3; under this change it would exit 1 (the old log), so the test was switched to other arguments.
fix_hint: Add `--again` to cmd_gate (refused together with nothing else) and an `again: bool = False` to run() that skips both
reuses; in finished_red skip exit 127 and exit >= 128; when a red is reused, print "gate: the code is unchanged since the

3. A log that ends exit 127 (command could not start) or exit >= 128 (killed by a signal) is not reused: a plain rerun
4. Green reuse is unchanged: HEAD = record commit of a green gate prints exit 0 and runs nothing.
5. HEAD = record commit + a change in lib/: full run (counter 2), as test_a_rerun_after_a_change_outside_the_checks_folder.

details: CONFIRMED by reading: after the wait only reusable() is asked (line ~364), finished_red() is not. Not wrong (the refusal
is quick and the rerun then reuses the red), but it is one extra round for the runner the item set out to save.
evidence: lib/relay_gate.py:364-367: green = ... reusable(worktree, now, command); if now != head: raise GateRefused(... "run it again")
failing_case: Gate A runs on G; gate B (same command) starts and waits on the worktree lock. A ends exit 1 and commits its log
(HEAD = R). B takes the lock: reusable(now) finds no green, now != head, so B raises "moved to another commit while the
gate waited: run it again". Should, now that a red is reusable: B reports A's red (exit 1) at once.
fix_hint: After the green check inside the slot: red = None if license_lines else finished_red(worktree, now, command); if red: return red.
